title: Cohomology and quotient maps of a two-term integral coefficient complex
statement:
Let $\ell$ be a prime, $\Omega$ an algebraically closed field, and $X=\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$. Work on a small skeleton of $X_{\mathrm{proet}}$ in the coefficient universe [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, def-weil-size-convention]. Let $p_X^*$ be the inverse image from the condensed point [sk-def-sfb-pullback-from-point], and put $R=p_X^*\underline{\mathbf Z_\ell}$ and $B_n=p_X^*\underline{\mathbf Z/\ell^n\mathbf Z}$ for $n\ge1$, with their quotient maps. The underlined rings are the continuous-function condensed rings, and these are the pulled-back coefficient rings [def-weil-l-adic-numbers, sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring, sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]. Use the canonical finite discrete ring identifications of [lem-pe-condensed-point-discrete-constant-comparisons]. Let $k_X$ be the constant $\mathbf F_\ell$-module sheaf [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf], acted on by $B_n$ through reduction modulo $\ell$. Use sheaf modules and sheaf tensor [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product].

Let $P=[R\xrightarrow{\ell}R]$ in cochain degrees $-1,0$, zero elsewhere [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules], and $K=Q_R(P)$ in the unbounded derived category [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Then $P$ is K-flat [def-pc-kflat-complex], its derived reduction $K_n=K\otimes_R^L B_n$ [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings] is represented by $P_n=[B_n\xrightarrow{\ell}B_n]$, and the canonical quotient transition $K_{n+1}\to K_n$ is represented by reduction in both terms. There are $B_n$-linear identifications
$$H^{-1}(K_n)\cong k_X,\qquad H^0(K_n)\cong k_X,\qquad H^q(K_n)=0\quad(q\notin\{-1,0\}).$$
The first identification is the inverse of the map induced, before $p_X^*$, by $\bar a\mapsto\ell^{n-1}a\bmod\ell^n$; the second is induced by reduction modulo $\ell$. Under these identifications the transition on $H^{-1}$ is zero and the transition on $H^0$ is the identity. Moreover $k_X\ne0$, and the canonical action map is an isomorphism
$$H^{-1}(K_{n+1})\otimes_{B_{n+1}}B_n\xrightarrow{\sim}k_X,$$
where the left side uses sheaf tensor and its map to $k_X$ sends $x\otimes b$ to $\bar b x$ after the specified degree-minus-one identification. Thus the map from this tensor product to $H^{-1}(K_n)$ induced by the quotient transition is zero.

source.place: Final paragraph: cohomology need not form an ordinary normalized tower. Explicit two-term calculation extracted from the agent proof; K-flat reduction uses Stacks Tag 06YY, lemma-derived-base-change.
